key_insight: The paper builds a benchmarking framework that maps realistic nuclear many-body Hamiltonians to qubit Hamiltonians and compares quantum resource needs across multiple eigensolver approaches.
engineering_relevance: It helps quantum algorithm designers assess whether nuclear simulation problems are feasible on future hardware by quantifying T-gate and system-size scaling under different model-space and interaction choices.
method: Map nuclear interactions in second quantization to qubit Hamiltonians using chiral EFT-based Hamiltonians.
Construct benchmark instances for no-core and valence-space settings with NN and selected 3N interactions.
Estimate resources for QPE, Quantum Krylov, and Observable DMD using Trotterization, qubitization, and QSVT primitives.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative resource estimates, especially T-gate counts and system size scaling, across algorithms and benchmark classes rather than experimental runtime data.
watch_item: The framework is benchmark-focused and depends on model-space and interaction truncation choices, so results may not directly generalize to full-scale nuclear calculations or near-term devices.
paper_title: Nuclear Many-Body Systems as Benchmarks for Quantum Computing
